You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

In observed examples, a tile containing exactly one 8 becomes its background color; a tile containing two 8 markers becomes color 1. Example 11x11 with 3x3 tiles separated by zero lines: output 3x3 all background 5 except the one tile with two 8s becomes 1. A 19x11 grid with 4x3 tiles separated by color-2 lines yielded a 4x3 output preserving background 0 except two double-8 tiles became 1. Treat separator lines as structural and use tile counts; validated on one demonstration and a correctly solved test. Do not assume behavior for zero or >2 markers without evidence.', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T07:10:02.097627+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T07:10:02.097646+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_mirror_repeat_grid_expansion_3x2', kind='memory', title='ARC mirror-repeat grid expansion 3x2', content='For this ARC task family, an H×W input grid A becomes a (3H)×(2W) output. Form the vertical row sequence as reverse(A rows) + A rows + reverse(A rows). For each row r in that sequence, output reverse(r) concatenated with r. Thus horizontal reflection is on the left of the original, and vertical tiling is bottom-to-top, top-to-bottom, bottom-to-top. Confirmed by demo 6×9→18×18 and constant 1×4→3×8; solved 9×3→27×6 by this rule.', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T06:52:19.225855+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T06:52:19.225874+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_7acf9041_expand_grid_into_four_rotations', kind='memory', title='ARC task-7acf9041: expand grid into four rotations', content='For recurring task-7acf9041, take the square input grid A (N×N) and make a 2N×2N output arranged as four rotated copies: top-left A unchanged; top-right A rotated 90° clockwise; bottom-left A rotated 90° counterclockwise; bottom-right A rotated 180°. Equivalently output blocks [[A, rot90(A, clockwise)], [rot90(A, counterclockwise), rot180(A)]]. Preserve all cell colors. Demonstrations: 15×15→30×30 and 13×13→26×26 confirmed the block arrangement; a 10×10 test was solved correctly with this rule. Confirmed again on task-7acf9041 with an 8×8 test: correctly produced a 16×16 output using the same four-quadrant rotation arrangement, solved with zero wrong submissions and no demo requests. Additional validation: demo showed a nonuniform 9×9 input producing an 18×18 grid with quadrants exactly [A, rotate 90° clockwise; rotate 90° counterclockwise, rotate 180°]. A test input of all color 5 at 11×11 correctly becomes a uniform 22×22 grid of 5s; even though rotations are visually indistinguishable in this degenerate case, still apply the 2×2 rotation-mosaic transformation.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T02:27:05.369455+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T06:17:42.139273+00:00', version=3), HarnessEntry(id='arc_tiled_grid_flag_tiles_with_exactly_two_markers', kind='memory', title='ARC tiled grid: flag tiles with exactly two markers', content="For ARC grids partitioned by full-width/full-height divider lines, inspect each rectangular tile and count its marker-colored cells. In this pattern, every tile's output cell is the original background color except tiles containing exactly two marker cells, which become color 1. Output dimensions equal the tile-array dimensions, preserving row/column order. Confirmed demo: 17x15 divided by color-5 lines into 3x4 tiles of size 5x3; each tile reduced to 1 if it held exactly two color-9 markers, otherwise background 6. Solved test: 23x14 divided by color-3 lines into 4x3 tiles of size 5x4; exactly-two-color-8 tiles became 1, others background 7. On new puzzles, infer geometry and colors, then count markers tile-by-tile.", path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T05:58:22.450145+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T05:58:33.404937+00:00', version=2), HarnessEntry(id='arc_2x2_rotational_mosaic_from_square_grid', kind='memory', title='ARC 2x2 rotational mosaic from square grid', content='For this Continual-ARC pattern, an n×n input grid A becomes a 2n×2n output formed by four rotated copies, not by nearest-neighbor pixel scaling. Partition output into n×n quadrants: top-left=A unchanged; top-right=rotate A 90° clockwise; bottom-left=rotate A 90° counterclockwise (270° clockwise); bottom-right=rotate A 180°. Equivalently, output = [[A, rot90cw(A)], [rot270cw(A), rot180(A)]]. Demos confirm: uniform 3×3 of 4 -> uniform 6×6 of 4; 1×1 [1] -> 2×2 of 1; informative 4×4 demo [[2,2,2,7],[4,2,9,0],[2,8,2,3],[6,5,1,2]] produced the four quadrants in those orientations. Avoid interpreting degenerate uniform demos as simple 2× scaling. On an 8×8 input, concatenate quadrant rows to form a 16×16 output. A distinctive 10×10 demo with background 6 and sparse colors 3,4,7,8,9 produced exactly these four rotations as quadrants, confirming the rule on a nonuniform case. Validated successfully on task-7acf9041 with a correct first submission. On a 13×13 input, concatenate quadrant rows to form a 26×26 output.', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T04:08:33.331290+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T05:51:39.318065+00:00', version=3), HarnessEntry(id='arc_separator_grid_count_repeated_markers', kind='memory', title='ARC separator-grid count repeated markers', content='For ARC inputs divided by full separator rows/columns into equal-sized panels, produce a compact grid with one output cell per panel. In each panel, ignore the separator color and treat the dominant panel background as background; count the non-background marker cells. Output 1 for panels containing at least two marker cells, and output the input background color for panels containing zero or one marker cell. Examples: 14x7 split by color-5 lines into 3x2 panels (each 4x3), background 4 and marker 7; output [[4,1],[4,1],[4,4]] when only top-right and middle-right panels have two markers. 9x9 split by color-3 separators into 2x2 panels (each 4x4), background 0, marker 5; output 1 in panels with >=2 markers and 0 otherwise. A 14x7 demo with background 7 and marker 4 output 1 only in the panel with two markers; output background was 7. Key: output blank cells use the panel/input background color, not a fixed 0 or marker color.', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T05:48:04.382286+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T05:48:04.382303+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_grid_intersections_fill_uniform_2x2_marked_corners', kind='memory', title='ARC grid intersections: fill uniform 2x2 marked corners', content='For ARC inputs with a regular grid of large uniform tiles and colored markers at grid-line intersections, extract the intersection-node matrix P (ignore intermediate tile pixels). The output is one cell per adjacent 2x2 block of nodes: output[r,c] is the marker color iff all four corners P[r,c], P[r,c+1], P[r+1,c], P[r+1,c+1] are the same special marker color; otherwise use the tile-interior fill color. The ordinary grid-line/background color at intersections is not a special marker and does not generate output. Output dimensions are (number of node rows−1) × (number of node columns−1); account for any outer padding or cropped boundary when locating the node lattice. Confirmed by two demos (0 markers on 8 grid background -> 5x5 output with 4 fill; several marker colors on 6 background -> 6x6 output with 1 fill) and a solved test (7/9 markers on 4 background -> 4x3 output with 1 fill).', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T05:47:13.466661+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T05:47:13.466677+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_compartment_pattern_copied_across_separator_grid', kind='memory', title='ARC compartment pattern copied across separator grid', content='For ARC grids divided by full separator lines, if a small demo shows a non-background pattern in one compartment copied unchanged into the corresponding empty compartment across a divider (e.g. 2×7 with a vertical color-4 separator: copy left-side motif to right-side at the same local coordinates), extend this to every same-sized compartment in the test grid when repeated vertical/horizontal separators form a tiled layout. Preserve separator and background colors; copy motif with its local orientation and coordinates in each compartment. Example: 13×23 with color-8 separators at row 6 and columns 7,15 makes six 6×7 compartments; pattern in upper-left is repeated at offsets (row 0 or 7, col 0,8,16) into all six compartments.', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T05:42:08.126207+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T05:42:08.126221+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_grid_clue_intersections_determine_output_cells', kind='memory', title='ARC grid clue intersections determine output cells', content='For Continual-ARC grids with a repeating rectangular tiled background and special colors at separator-line intersections, read the separator intersections as a coarse vertex-color matrix. Let X be the unmarked separator color and B the tile-interior fill. Crop to the rectangle spanning all clue-bearing vertices (cells != X), retaining every regular vertex between min/max clue rows and columns. Each adjacent-vertex rectangle gives one output cell: if its four corners all have the same color, emit that color; otherwise emit B. Dimensions are (selected vertex rows − 1) × (selected vertex columns − 1). Confirmed for task-53f0c104 on 27×27: separators every 4 rows and 5 columns, X=4, B=3; clue crop rows 4,8,12,16,20,24 and cols 9,14,19,24. The vertex matrix was [[4,9,9,4],[4,9,9,4],[2,2,7,7],[2,2,7,7],[7,7,1,1],[7,7,1,1]], yielding [[3,9,3],[3,3,3],[2,3,7],[3,3,3],[7,3,1]]. Another solved test of this pattern used X=0, B=9 and produced [[6,9,9,9,9,7],[6,6,9,3,9,7]]. Demonstrations validated corner unanimity; unanimous X corners also emit X. Do not include irrelevant outer intersections outside the clue bounding box or use X as the disagreement fill.', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T04:18:13.241285+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T04:49:30.749267+00:00', version=2), HarnessEntry(id='arc_mirrored_tripling_of_grid_dimensions', kind='memory', title='ARC mirrored tripling of grid dimensions', content='Continual-ARC pattern: given an HxW input grid, output has size 3H x 2W. Each output row is formed by concatenating the row reversed left-to-right, then the original row. The output row sequence is reversed(input rows) + input rows + reversed(input rows). Demonstrations: 5x4 became 15x8; 1x7 became 3x14. For the 1-row case, reversing the one-row sequence gives three identical output rows. Be precise: vertical order is [rows reversed, rows forward, rows reversed], not simply triplicate each input row; source rows at each of the three positions in each output block follow this sequence.\nValidated on recurring task-30861639: demo input 2x13 produced 6x26; output rows followed [reversed source-row order, source-row order, reversed source-row order], with each source row mapped to reverse(row)+row. Test 1x12 [5,0,1,3,4,3,7,6,9,3,2,8] correctly became three identical rows [8,2,3,9,6,7,3,4,3,1,0,5,5,0,1,3,4,3,7,6,9,3,2,8]. Thus HxW -> 3H x 2W; output row order is rows[::-1]+rows+rows[::-1], each row is reversed(row)+row; singleton-height input simply yields that one transformed row repeated thrice.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T03:17:52.501171+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T04:21:29.712062+00:00', version=2)]
